paragraphs.title: Education and background
paragraphs.text: My name is Ding Tao, and I was born in April 1998 in Guiyang, Guizhou Province. I am currently a PhD student at the Institute of Basic Medical Sciences, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College. Throughout my academic journey, I have maintained a passion and dedication to my major courses, which has led to outstanding achievements across various disciplines.

paragraphs.title: Research focus
paragraphs.text: Under the guidance of Professor Yang Juntao, my research focuses on the biological mechanisms underlying potential therapeutic targets for pulmonary fibrosis. I am currently conducting multi-omics studies of silica-induced silicosis and bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Both studies include drug treatment, and my work focuses on treatment responses, underlying molecular mechanisms, and potential therapeutic targets.

paragraphs.title: Research achievements
paragraphs.text: To date, I have published two papers as a first or co-first author. I was a co-first author of "Global profiling of protein lactylation in Caenorhabditis elegans," published in Proteomics, with an impact factor of 3.4. More recently, I was the first author of "The Mechanism of Omicron Variant-Associated Cardiac Injury in Rhesus Macaques Was Revealed by Proteomic and Phosphoproteomic Analyses," published in MedComm in 2025. I also received a first-class scholarship at Peking Union Medical College for the 2022-2023 academic year.

paragraphs.title: Core competencies
paragraphs.text: Through my scientific training, I have accumulated some key competencies.

paragraphs.title: Project design
paragraphs.text: I am well-versed in the design and conceptualization of proteomics projects and actively participate in the design and discussion of new research topics.

paragraphs.title: Instrument experience
paragraphs.text: I am capable of operating various liquid chromatography-mass spectrometers, such as the timsTOF Pro 2, independently, and I am able to perform maintenance and optimize mass spectrometry methods for different samples.

paragraphs.title: Data analysis and writing
paragraphs.text: I possess the ability to independently process proteomics and related multi-omics data and can write SCI papers independently.

paragraphs.title: Personal qualities
paragraphs.text: I have a cheerful personality and enjoy communication. I maintain a positive attitude in both academia and daily life. With a good mindset, solid professional skills, and relentless enthusiasm, I am confident that I can become an outstanding researcher.

paragraphs.title: Closing
paragraphs.text: Thank you all for your time and consideration.
